abstract:
Landau's Hauptsatz turns a growth bound $\zeta(s)\ll e^{\varphi(t)}$ on $\sigma\ge1-1/\psi(t)$ into a zero-free region $\sigma\ge1-c/(\psi(2t+1)\varphi(2t+1))$. It applies to every Beurling zeta function $\zeta=\exp\int x^{-s}dm$ with $dm\ge0$ and a simple pole at $1$. Tracking Landau's proof gives every $c<1/(8V)\approx0.0036$, and an earlier paper (riemann_hypothesis_93) showed that no $c$ above $0.4124$ works.

We show that for regular growth functions, $\psi(9t)\varphi(9t)\le(1+o(1))\psi(t)\varphi(t)$, every zero satisfies $(1-\beta)\psi(\gamma)\varphi(\gamma)\ge L-o(1)$ with $L=2\cos^2\theta/(S+\kappa)$. Here $\kappa=\limsup\log\psi/\varphi\le1$, and $\theta$ and $S$ come from a non-negative cosine polynomial. A polynomial of degree 46 found by Mossinghoff, Trudgian and Yang gives $L>0.0786$ for every $\kappa\le1$, and $L>0.1006$ at $\kappa=0$. The regular examples of the earlier paper attain every $\kappa\in[0,1)$. So for regular growth functions the best constant lies in $[0.0786,0.4124]$, a window of factor $5.2$ instead of $114$. For growth functions with $1/u=o(f(u))$ these examples answer negatively the question of Broucke and Révész whether $c=1$ for every admissible pair, and their refined guess $1/(1+\alpha)$.

In Vinogradov-Korobov form, with the growth bound $|\zeta(\sigma+it)|\le At^{B(1-\sigma)_+^{3/2}}\log^{2/3}t$, the same argument gives $1-\beta\ge(0.0561B^{-2/3}-o(1))(\log\gamma)^{-2/3}(\log\log\gamma)^{-1/3}$. Mossinghoff, Trudgian and Yang proved this constant for the Riemann zeta function, using zero-density estimates as well. The earlier paper's ceiling for this class is $0.250B^{-2/3}$.

The proof is Ford's version of Heath-Brown's method. The inputs that are special to the Riemann zeta function (functional equation, zero counts, finite order) are replaced by Jensen's formula and the Borel-Carathéodory lemma on discs of radius $1/\psi$. A discretised linear programme gives numerical evidence that Heath-Brown's kernel is optimal among product kernels $b_jf$.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary: Version 4 is the narrower update asked for in the review of version 3. Against the accepted version 2, Theorem 1, its proof and every constant are unchanged. (1) Proposition 7.1 now covers kappa_0 in [0,1) instead of (0,1). For kappa_0 = 0 the examples use A = tau^{-1} log^2(1/f), so log psi = o(phi); like the examples for kappa_0 > 0, they rely on [9, Sec. 3, Step 2], which needs 1/u = o(f(u)). Corollary 2 is stated for 0 <= kappa <= 1, and Section 7 notes that at kappa = 0 the window is [0.1006, 0.4124]. (2) New Remark 7.3 compares Theorem 1 with Broucke and Revesz, arXiv:2611.03356 (new reference [13]). As the review asked, the comparison is restricted to the common admissible range: Theorem 1 needs psi << e^phi, which [13] does not assume, so the remark treats alpha < 1, and alpha = 1 with psi << e^phi assumed. The remark checks that the examples of Proposition 7.1 lie in their class, so for growth functions with 1/u = o(f(u)) the n = 6 data answer their question c = 1 and their refined guess 1/(1+alpha) negatively for alpha in [0,1). It also notes that their Theorem 3.1 prints c > where c < is meant. (3) Section 1 and the abstract gain one sentence each on these points. Proposition 7.4 of version 3 (the classical-width pairs of Diamond, Montgomery and Vorhauer) and every claim that depends on it have been removed. That construction will be submitted separately.
title: The constant in Landau's zero-free region theorem is at least 0.078 for regular growth functions
